title: Contributor Onboarding and Role Alignment Roadmap
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook provides a unified onboarding roadmap and a practical role-alignment framework for contributors joining Redwood. It combines hiring touchpoints, preboarding and 12-month ramp milestones, role templates, benefits enrollment steps, and a compact tools-access matrix so new hires (and their managers) have a single reference for rapid, measurable impact.

Purpose:
- Accelerate time-to-productivity while ensuring clear expectations for role scope and career trajectory.
- Reduce uneven experiences across teams by standardizing core checkpoints, account provisioning, and benefits sign-up.
- Provide reusable templates (role responsibilities, RACI, ramp goals) that managers and people-ops can use during offers and 1:1s.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time employees and long-term contractors (>6 months) across engineering, product, go-to-market, and support functions.
- Does not replace team-specific technical onboarding or project ramp docs — instead it layers consistent people and tools processes.

Quick Start Checklist (for hiring manager within 7 days of offer acceptance):
1) Confirm new hire start date and send Welcome Guide email.
2) Confirm role template and 30/60/90 goals in Lattice (or linked HR system).
3) Request tool provisioning: SSO groups, Slack channel, code repo access, CI/CD pipelines, ticketing queue.
4) Assign buddy and schedule 1st-week sync calendar invites.
5) Provide benefits enrollment instructions and deadlines.

Onboarding Phases and Key Activities:
- Preboarding (2 weeks before start):
  - People-ops sends Welcome Guide + benefits packet and equity explanation.
  - Manager creates 30/60/90 draft and shares with candidate.
  - IT requests accounts: SSO, Okta group, email, Git repo, VPN, cloud console role. Example CLI to request infra account (internal tooling):
    $ rdw-provision create-account --email newhire@example.com --team core-platform --roles dev,read-only-cloud
  - Assign buddy and schedule first-day intro meeting.

- Week 0–1 (orientation & baseline):
  - Day 1: Company orientation (mission, product surfaces, security overview).
  - Day 2–5: Team-level deep dives, codebase walkthrough, first small deliverable.
  - Complete mandatory training: security phishing, data handling, D&I.

- Month 1–3 (ramp & early delivery):
  - Complete two small cross-functional tickets and one customer-oriented review.
  - Monthly 1:1s focused on blockers, access, and role clarity.
  - Manager verifies access matrix and removes temporary escalations.

- Month 3–6 (expanding scope):
  - Lead a medium-sized feature or operational improvement.
  - Career conversation: document preferred growth path (IC / manager / specialist) and update competency map.

- Month 6–12 (stabilize & growth):
  - Deliver measurable outcome (reduced latency, feature adoption %, cost improvement).
  - Prepare performance calibration packet and goals for next cycle.

Role Alignment Framework (how we define and communicate roles):
- Each role at Redwood uses a compact template with these fields:
  - Role name, Level, Core responsibilities (3–6 bullets), Success metrics (KPIs), Primary stakeholders, Typical ramp milestones.
- Example: Senior ML Engineer (L4) Responsibilities:
  - Lead inference optimization projects, reduce P99 latency for core models by 15% in 6 months.
  - Mentor junior engineers and run design reviews.
  - Own rollout and canary rules for model-serving changes.

RACI snapshot (example for a typical feature rollout):
| Activity | Responsible | Accountable | Consulted | Informed |
| Design spec | Eng owner | Product manager | Research | All-team |
| Infra changes | Eng infra | Eng infra lead | Security | Customer Success |
| Release / Canary | Eng owner | Eng manager | SRE | Stakeholders |

Templates (copy/paste friendly):
- 30/60/90 goals (short):
  30 days: Complete codebase and observability setup; merge first PR.
  60 days: Deliver feature X; own a small oncall rotation.
  90 days: Lead an improvement and present outcomes.

- Role responsibilities (three-line):
  - Focus area: Inference serving stability and performance.
  - Outcome: Reduce inference cost per 1M tokens while maintaining quality.
  - KPI: Cost per token, P95 latency, regression alerts per 100K responses.

Benefits and Perks Enrollment (practical steps):
- Health & dental: Enroll within 30 days of start via Payroll portal. Submit coverage choices and dependent info.
- 401(k): Auto-enroll default is 3% — change in Benefits portal.
- Parental leave: Submit notice to people-ops 60 days prior to expected leave when possible.
- Wellness stipend and remote office allowance: Submit receipts in Expensely within 90 days.

Key deadlines (summary):
- Benefits enrollment: 30 days from start.
- Equity grant acceptance: 14 days from offer (ask people-ops if extension needed).
- Tax/Payroll forms: Before first payroll run.

Tools Access Matrix (core tools and baseline permissions):
| Tool | Default Group | Typical Permissions | Request path |
| Slack | all-employees | Member | Auto-provision via Okta |
| GitHub | team-{slug} | Write to team repos | Manager requests via rdw-access |
| Cloud Console | project-{team} | Read / deploy for core infra | infra-provision CLI |
| Datadog | observability | Dashboards: read/write | Observability oncall |

Note: managers must verify and remove any staging or emergency escalations at Month 1 review to minimize blast radius.

Hiring & Offer Handoffs (touchpoints and responsibilities):
1) Recruiter: candidate screening, offer details, background check initiation.
2) Hiring manager: role template, 30/60/90 draft, final interviews, offer acceptance plan.
3) People-ops: benefits packet, payroll setup, equity documentation.
4) IT/Infra: account provisioning queue.

Suggested checklists for a smooth handoff (recruiter -> manager -> people-ops):
- Recruiter confirms salary band and any relocation/visa notes.
- Manager confirms team orientation schedule and primary projects.
- People-ops verifies starter kit (laptop, stipend, parking if applicable).

Ramp Metrics and Success Criteria (measurable SLOs for onboarding):
- Time-to-first-merge: target median 7 days.
- Time-to-independent-deploy: median 45 days for technical roles.
- Completed mandatory trainings: 100% by Day 14.
- Manager 1:1 satisfaction score: >4/5 at Month 2 pulse.

Escalation Path and Contacts:
- Immediate issues (access, payroll errors): people-ops@redwood.com (24–48h SLT).
- Security incidents during onboarding: security-oncall@redwood.com and SRE pager.
- Benefits questions: benefits@redwood.com.

Ownership and Review Cadence:
- People-ops owns the playbook and quarterly review cadence.
- Managers are responsible for executing the checklist and filing completion in the onboarding tracker.
- Quarterly metrics review: people-ops + hiring managers + eng leadership.

Appendix A — Sample role YAML (for role templates stored in team repo):

role_name: "senior-ml-engineer"
level: "L4"
responsibilities:
  - "Optimize inference pipelines; own KPIs"
  - "Mentor junior engineers"
success_metrics:
  - "p95_latency_reduction: 15%"
  - "token_cost_reduction: 10%"
primary_contacts:
  - "engineering-manager@example.com"
  - "people-ops@example.com"

Appendix B — Useful links:
- Onboarding toolchain and access guide (internal): /confluence/company-handbook/05_internal-tools/onboarding-toolchain-access-and-career-checkpoints-2025
- Role competency maps: /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027
- Benefits portal: https://payroll.redwood.internal/benefits

Notes and iteration log:
- 2024-08-19: Initial draft (Aisha Patel).
- 2024-11-06: Added tools access matrix and CLI example (Diego Morales).
- 2025-02-03: Updated ramp metrics & deadlines; published.

If you are a manager preparing for a new hire this week: use this document as your canonical checklist, copy the role YAML into the team repo, and ping people-ops with the onboarding tracker ID. If anything in this playbook is missing or causes friction, add an inline comment or nominate a reviewer for the next quarterly revision.
